findings.title: Local review can drive two fix rounds
findings.description: The local-review branch in `Run.work` takes its fix round from the same `attempts` counter as the failed-check and pull-request-review rounds, which starts at `FIX_ATTEMPTS = 2`. Each blocking local review does `attempts -= 1` and then `continue`, so two consecutive local reviews with findings can each start the agent, and only the local review spends the budget. The test `test_an_open_local_finding_after_the_rounds_needs_a_human_with_no_commit` confirms this: three agent starts, two of them driven by local findings. The PR description and the ticket-derived rule allow one local fix round per run, separate from the two pull-request rounds, so the code allows more review-driven fix rounds than the limit.

findings.title: Unreviewed staged edits reach the commit
findings.description: `commit()` compares the clone's index tree with `reviewed` once, then invokes `git commit` using that same mutable index in a separate command. An agent-left background process can change an in-scope file and stage it after the comparison but before the commit; the later status check sees the resulting commit as clean.

findings.title: Commits can skip the actual local review
findings.description: `work()` passes a snapshot captured before `local_review()` to `commit()`, while Qodo reviews the live clone rather than that snapshot. If a background process changes a file while Qodo reads it and restores it before the comparison, the comparison passes even though the committed tree is not the tree Qodo reviewed.

findings.title: Unreviewed edits can enter the commit
findings.description: `Run.work` calls `local_review()` and then `commit()` without verifying that the files and staged tree still match the snapshot taken before review. An agent can leave a background process running after its start ends; if that process changes an in-scope file after Qodo collects the diff, the runner stages and commits the new contents without reviewing them.

findings.title: Open findings lack handoff checks
findings.description: The new timeout test ends with `self.fail(...)` or returns from its loop before the following handoff assertions, so those assertions never execute. When a local finding remains open after its fix round, the preceding test therefore does not verify that the handoff identifies the uncommitted work and lists the open finding.

findings.title: Timed-out reviews leave helpers running
findings.description: `local_review` invokes Qodo through `sh()`, whose timeout kills only the Qodo process, not any child processes it started. If Qodo has a helper running when the ten-minute limit expires, that helper can continue after the run stops and retain access to the review worktree.

findings.title: Pull request body can exceed GitHub's size limit
findings.description: `build_pr_body` adds every agent report, fenced and capped at 20000 characters each. The cap was sized for at most 3 agent starts ("3 reports of 20000 fit"), but the local round adds a 4th start, so a run that uses the local round plus both fix attempts can produce a body of about 80000 characters, above GitHub's 65536 limit. When that happens, `gh pr create` or the PATCH of the body in `push()` fails and the run ends `needs-human` after a fix commit was already pushed.

findings.title: Local review adds an extra fix round
findings.description: `LOCAL_FIX_ATTEMPTS = 1` gives the local Qodo review its own agent round, and `local_attempts` is checked separately from `attempts` in `Run.work`. The pull request review can still spend its 2 rounds, so one run can start the agent 3 times for review findings, which the checklist forbids for blocking review findings. A local threshold finding that comes back after the local round is also committed rather than sent to the shared budget.

findings.title: Bad finding IDs abandon the handoff
findings.description: `local_review` inserts an unchecked JSON `id` into `local_seen`, although `check_finding` does not validate that field. An array or object ID raises `TypeError` after the review succeeds, escaping the `ValueError` handler and ending the runner through its top-level error path rather than its `needs-human` handoff; absent IDs with identical titles also collapse distinct findings into one count.

findings.title: Local reviews receive GitHub tokens
findings.description: `local_review` launches Qodo with `GIT_ENV`, but `sh` overlays that mapping on the runner's entire environment rather than restricting credentials. When the runner uses an environment-provided GitHub token, the new review process receives it while inspecting agent-modified repository content, unlike the agent process from which those tokens are explicitly removed.

findings.title: Local informational findings go unlisted
findings.description: `local_review` unpacks `sort_findings(review)` into `blocking, flagged, _, _` and keeps only `blocking`, so open informational local findings are used for a log count and then discarded, and dismissed ones are dropped at the same line. The handoff built from `local_summary` lists only `self.local_open`, so a person reading the handoff never sees those findings. The pull request review's `self.flagged` and `self.dismissed` are unaffected, so this gap only affects local-review results.

findings.title: Open local findings can be counted as fixed
findings.description: `local_review` builds its open list only from `review["findings"]` through `sort_findings`. It never checks that each id in `finding_state.still_open` and `finding_state.introduced` is present in that list. Qodo documents that on repeated (incremental) reviews the `findings` array may hold only this call's findings, with older engines putting full objects in the buckets. In that case a finding that is still open drops out of `local_open`, is reported as "fixed" in the pull request body, and breaks the runner's rule that an unknown shape is never read as clean.

findings.title: Dismissed local findings appear fixed
findings.description: `local_summary` calculates fixed findings as every previously seen finding that is absent from the last open list, regardless of its final status. If a later review marks a finding `dismissed` or `outdated`, the pull request body and issue handoff report it as fixed even though no fix was established.

findings.title: A full revert in the local round gives a misleading reason
findings.description: When the agent undoes all of its changes in the local round of the first iteration, the second `local_review` call runs `qodo review` on a tree with no commits and no changes. Qodo answers with `error: no local changes vs merge-base` (the `local-review-no-changes.json` fixture), so the run stops with "the Qodo local review did not run". The intended "no change is left to commit after the round for the local review" branch is never reached on that path, and the person reading the handoff is pointed at a tool failure that did not happen.

findings.title: Acceptance criteria go into the wrong context field
findings.description: `local_context` puts the ticket title and every acceptance criterion into `recent_work`. Qodo defines that field as the changes since the previous review and uses `notes` for requirements. The same text is sent on the round-2 review too, so the reviewer is never told what the agent changed in its fix round and reads requirements as though they were work already done.
